rule: A window of width W years is the half-open JD interval [a, a + 365.25 W) (4.6). A named window below runs from 0 h UT+2 of 1 Jan of its first year to 0 h UT+2 of 1 Jan after its last year, half-open; a candidate is inside if its UT+2 Day 0 (day0_jdn_ut2) is.

reproduction.source: 1250-1115 BC, 136 years: B&M's search window [B&M; win 9] (4.6)

background.source: 4.1: -1999-01-01 to +200-12-31 (2,200 Julian years), from the first year of NASA's elements

core.source: 4.1: targets lie at least 251 years inside B, so every window of every width lies inside it

data_margins.source: 4.1: the 40-day clue offsets and the +/-60-day Mercury searches

null_window_range.source: 6.3.2 [r3v7 R3-7]: I16(a)'s 21 null windows per counted set lie within -1000..+300, each so that every event the set's rows can link to, at the set's longest link or day offset in either direction, lies inside -1999..+300

epoch_band.source: 4.2, 7.2: P_BM,E and P_MWRA,E, Day 0 (UT+2) within +/-700 years of the target's year

epoch_band_halves.source: 7.2: Q_exch's drift tests inside the band

p8_ends.source: 8.2 P8: the first and last 700 years of the background (7.2 notes the difference from the epoch band)

widths.source: 5.3 F7 (136 BM; 91, 251 DOC); 5.1 item 5; 6.3.1 and 6.4 (136); 6.5 (the Odyssey's two windows)

negatives.source: 6.5: each clean negative is searched in the Odyssey's own two windows at its own site; twenty further random positions per width are a sensitivity (seeds.json)

controls.positions: the harness places the anchor's accepted date at a uniformly random position (seeds.json, per set), plus twenty further positions as a sensitivity; I16(a)'s 21 null windows per counted set lie in null_window_range
